chunks: And that which was narrated is - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Murrah, the freedman of Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who throws off a louse, so he said: 'Throw it off, may God distance it, not censured and not lost.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.وَلَا مَفْقُودَةٍ: And not lost / not missing (implying no penalty due)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in ihram who kills a louse?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of minor disruptions to ihram, specifically the removal of a louse, by affirming that such an act is neither blameworthy (*ghayr mahmuda*) nor resulting in the loss of reward (*la mafquda*). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between intentional transgression and accidental or minor acts that do not incur the full penalty of kafarah. The ruling underscores the principle of ease (*yusr*) in ritual purity and consecration, ensuring that insignificant disturbances do not unduly burden the pilgrim.
